week_focus: Design a small reusable open-top pouch for three paper prompt cards, each 60mm by 80mm. Compare generic felt, woven cotton and knit using actual sample tests or clearly labelled model information. The original fabric photo shows appearance only; it does not prove stretch, firmness, edge behaviour or pupil testing. Compare hand running stitch, approved fabric adhesive bonding and optional generic fastenings. A fastening closes an opening and does not replace joined sides and bottom. Default plan: two 100mm by 120mm pieces,10mm seam lines on left, right and bottom, top open, hand running stitch. Record the pupil’s own choice and any approved adaptation.
evidence_rule: Actual pupil choices, work, support, dates and comments only. Adult models, photo descriptions and simulations are labelled honestly. Missing work or unperformed practical actions stay visible. A tick records weekly evidence, not award completion.

fabric_image_prompt: Use case: scientific-educational. Asset type: original generic fabric swatch comparison strip for a secondary school design and technology lesson. Make a wide 3:1 landscape image with three equal panels separated by clean white gutters, neutral overhead studio lighting, realistic close-up illustration. Panel one: a plain medium blue felt square with a dense softly fuzzy surface and flat clean cut edges. Panel two: a pale ochre plain woven cotton square with visible perpendicular warp and weft threads and a short lightly fraying cut edge. Panel three: a muted grey stretchy knitted jersey square with fine knitted loops and a gently curled cut edge. Each swatch lies alone, flat enough to compare, on a simple off-white background. No implied testing or numerical strength/stretch claims; these are invented teaching illustrations, not learner evidence. Age-appropriate for14–16 year olds, practical and uncluttered, texture clearly distinguishable. No people, hands, tools, fastenings, packaging, products, brands, logos, watermark, letters, text, labels, numbers or decorative icons. Keep fabric edges visible and composition spacious.
